pool.text: Peter de Bermingham obtained a charter to hold a market at his castle.
Birmingham established a commercial market for agricultural produce by royal charter.
Bishop Vesey founded Bishop Vesey's Grammar School in the city.
King Edward VI founded King Edward's School, Birmingham.
Abraham Darby I built the first blast furnace to smelt iron ore.
Lewis Paul and John Wyatt invented roller spinning for mechanised cotton.
The Birmingham Film Society was established with an inaugural screening.
Otto Frisch and Rudolf Peierls described how a practical nuclear weapon could be constructed.
Birmingham Corporation Tramways closed its substantial tram system.
The former Birmingham Central Library opened as a large municipal library.
A series of bomb attacks in two pubs killed twenty-one people.
The first dedicated comedy club outside London, The Glee Club, opened.
The Tyseley Energy from Waste Plant was built as a large incineration plant.
Birmingham hosted the 24th G8 summit.
Trams returned to the city with the West Midlands Metro operating services.
Birmingham began hosting the Frankfurt Christmas Market as an outdoor market.
The Birmingham Comedy Festival started taking place in October.
The Big City Plan aimed to move the city into the top global index.
The biennial Birmingham International Dance Festival started, organised by DanceXchange.
Bournville College opened its campus in Longbridge.
